requirements.title: BIT_SIZE permits scalar or array integer arguments
requirements.definition: The I argument to BIT_SIZE may be a scalar or an array.

pending.bit_size-array-argument-permitted: Call BIT_SIZE([1,2]) and assign the result to an integer scalar initialized to -777; assert the same positive value as BIT_SIZE(1), proving the array actual is admitted while the result remains scalar.

requirements.title: BIT_SIZE returns the bit-model length z
requirements.definition: The BIT_SIZE result is the value of the number of bits z of the integer bit model defined for bit manipulation contexts in 16.3.

pending.bit_size-result-model-z: For each integer kind exercised by the fixture (at least default integer, plus a guarded selected_int_kind(18) kind when available), set z=BIT_SIZE(0_kind) from a -777 sentinel and assert z>1. Keep the exact shift-out check SHIFTL(1_kind,z) == 0_kind. For the leftmost retained bit, stay in bit context rather than observing the processor-dependent numeric value: assert BTEST(SHIFTL(1_kind,z-1),z-1) is .true. and BTEST(SHIFTL(1_kind,z-1),z-2) is .false. 16.9.187 defines SHIFTL in terms of ISHFT; 16.9.113 says left shifts lose bits shifted out and shift zeros in; 16.9.50 tests the bit at POS. Replacing BIT_SIZE with KIND or z-1 makes at least one BTEST/shift-out relation wrong instead of merely reusing BIT_SIZE as its own oracle.
